title: Signal Catalog Entry
description: A signal in a signal catalog: identity, name and description, type, provider, coverage, deployments, and pricing options.

signal_id.description: DEPRECATED. Use signal_ref instead. Legacy SignalId retained for compatibility with older Signals Protocol clients.

signal_ref.description: Canonical signal reference for discovery, activation, and media-buy targeting. Provider-published signals use scope 'data_provider'. Source-native custom signals that are not published in adagents.json signals[] use scope 'signal_source'. Product-local refs are only meaningful when the response is explicitly scoped to a product context.

signal_agent_segment_id.description: Opaque resolved-segment handle issued by this signal source. Pass this string verbatim to activate_signal.signal_agent_segment_id, and echo it in package signal targeting when the selected product option exposes the same handle. Treat the value as provider-scoped and opaque: providers MAY namespace it so two providers can expose similarly named signals without relying on a shared taxonomy. Do not pass the signal_id object as this handle, and do not reconstruct a segment handle from categorical values when get_signals returned a resolved segment.

value_type.description: The data type of this signal's values (binary, categorical, numeric)

categories.description: Valid values for categorical signals. Present when value_type is 'categorical'. Buyers must use one of these values in SignalTargeting.values.

range.description: Valid range for numeric signals. Present when value_type is 'numeric'.

signal_type.description: Commercial/provenance type of signal (marketplace, custom, owned)

data_provider.description: Human-readable source name for the signal, when applicable. For data_provider-scoped signals this is the data provider name; for signal_source-scoped signals it may identify the signal source or proprietary origin.

coverage_percentage.description: DEPRECATED for detailed planning. Optional legacy scalar percentage of audience coverage retained only as a fallback for clients that do not consume coverage_forecast. When coverage_forecast is present, coverage_forecast is authoritative for signal-level discovery and coverage_percentage is fallback-only. If coverage_forecast includes an absent bucket over the same denominator, coverage_percentage SHOULD align with 100 * (1 - absent coverage_rate.mid).

coverage_forecast.description: Optional forecast-shaped signal availability guidance. When present, this is authoritative for signal-level discovery coverage. Use this to disclose the denominator, bucket semantics, not-present bucket, aggregate present bucket, and per-value coverage distribution for the signal.

signal_status.description: Construction readiness of this signal: 'processing' (still being built, for example a custom or lookalike segment derived from a seed audience), 'ready', or 'failed'. Absent means 'ready', so agents that do not build segments on demand are unchanged. Agents MUST NOT report is_live: true or return an activation_key for a signal that is not 'ready'. Buyers SHOULD NOT call activate_signal for, or target in create_media_buy, a signal whose signal_status is 'processing' or 'failed'. Agents that emit 'processing' or 'failed' and return wholesale_feed_version MUST change it when a signal's signal_status changes; the rule binds only agents that emit those values. Distinct from the response's top-level status discriminator. Experimental (x-status: experimental): part of the signals.signal_lifecycle surface — agents that emit signal_status MUST list signals.signal_lifecycle in experimental_features. Per docs/reference/experimental-status, this surface MAY change between 3.x releases with notice. See docs/signals/tasks/get_signals for the re-read and Submitted-arm rules.

source_audience_id.description: Seed audience this signal was derived from, for example a lookalike or custom segment built from a first-party seed. When present, this is the audience_id the buyer synced with sync_audiences (typically audience_type 'lookalike_seed') on the same account, at the agent that holds the seed. Lineage only: AdCP does not transport seed membership through get_signals, and the audience remains governed by its sync_audiences consent and residency terms. Agents MUST NOT return it to a caller that did not supply an account, or in a response with cache_scope 'public', because the value is buyer-scoped. Experimental (x-status: experimental): part of the signals.signal_lifecycle surface. Per docs/reference/experimental-status, this surface MAY change between 3.x releases with notice.

pricing_options.description: Pricing options available for this signal when it has an incremental price. The buyer selects one and passes its pricing_option_id in report_usage or package-level signal_targeting_groups for billing verification. Omit when pricing is unavailable to the caller, bundled into the destination product, or has no incremental cost.
